item.text: I’m checking the current API shape before I touch anything. The remaining useful refactor is to stop leaking concrete mutable collections from every method and make the codebook/results immutable, which will tighten the design without changing output.

I found a concrete improvement to the API: every method still returns a mutable `ArrayList`, and `Codebook` rebuilds fresh lists on every read. I’m tightening that by switching the surface to `List<String>` and freezing the codebook outputs once at build time.

The API now returns `List` and the codebook snapshots are frozen once instead of being recopied on every accessor call. I’m adding one test to lock in that immutability contract before re-running the suite.
I’ve finished the refactor and test update. I’m compiling and running the demo plus the test harness to verify the new immutable-return contract didn’t change behavior.

Refactored [HuffmanCoding.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/033_huffman_coding/HuffmanCoding.java:13) so the public API returns `List<String>` instead of concrete mutable `ArrayList`s. I also changed `Codebook` to freeze its traversal-order and symbol-order views once during construction, so repeated reads do not allocate fresh copies and callers cannot mutate the returned results.

I updated [HuffmanCodingTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/033_huffman_coding/HuffmanCodingTest.java:5) with an immutability check for both code views.
